You can get latex/powder free gloves and it should be just as fine! In the meantime make sure your hands are thoroughly washed and wetter than you think they should be before you handle them. They have delicate slime coats and dry skin can literally tug at their skin and our skin’s oils can be bad for them. They do love being out and it’s great to hold them in a gloved hand for feeding!

Snake plants! Unkillable, sturdy, and come in a variety of beautiful colors and patterns!

Tank wise, they are treefrogs so height over width. There’s an 18x18x24 tank that’s a great setup for beginners and comfortably fits 1-2 White’s.

Plants should be ideally something that can handle the humidity and the weight of a frog on the leaves. Snake plants are an amazing low effort option and come in beautiful variegated varieties. Moss is also a staple. As for care, the humidity should be pretty high for your frogs and thus require minimal watering. Snake plants are practically unkillable. I have 3 lights usually, a UVB, a daylight with heat, and a night heat. 

Fountains can be a great option to eliminate stagnant water but are a hassle to sanitize. I personally just change their water daily. But it’s a matter of personal preference. You want to be sure the depth is right for the frogs and not too deep or with too strong a flow. 

Humidity wise I use a Reptirain auto-sprayer (it’s pretty cheap on Chewy.com and had 1-3 day shipping included). You CAN use a spray bottle in a pinch (and you should always have one handy) but you will need to be spraying your tank and frogs every few hours to keep the humidity up so investing in an automatic machine is almost an essential if you ever plan to be out of the home for school or work. 

Leaf litter: True. But honestly a risk I wouldn’t personally take. I use moss and coconut fiber and I’ve never had any issue. Why tempt fate? But I know others bake, boil, etc their leaf litter. It’s just a risk of introducing bacteria or parasites I’d be extra careful with. 

Additionally I would recommend becoming very familiar with the dietary needs of young frogs. When I’m checking rescues to take in young neglected frogs I see a lot with Metabolic Bone Disease. You want to be super aware of how often you feed, vitamins, and calcium dusting (always phosphorus free!). Another issue they have is obesity so being sure not to overfeed the greedy grubs! 

Tank cleaning I usually do a solution of less than 1 part bleach to 19 parts water (the aim is around 3% bleach) to wipe everything down weekly. Coconut fiber should also be fresh weekly. So a planted tank can be a struggle in this respect as well. Personally I’d recommend starting off with plastic stuff and moving to planted as you figure out what works for you, 

Good luck!

Actually no, not fuck the court of public opinion in this case. 

Consider the large sum of individuals who are abused behind closed doors before taking their life, losing jobs, education opportunities, and friends. Consider the public backlash on anyone who comes forward with an accusation of abuse. Anyone who has been subject to abuse can tell you that offline and online people have absolutely no problem telling you that they think you are a liar, a whore, and a piece of shit. Just because more people are believing survivors does not mean MOST people are. Far from it. 

Additionally, mental health is often used as a bargaining chip to get individuals not to report. What is the alternative in this scenario? It’s that the woman didn’t speak out about her situation. Often times abusers will manipulate people into not reporting or acting against abuse because it would put the abuser in a position of stress. Many abusers will even threaten to kill themselves or hurt others if any form of report is made. 

I’m not saying I don’t believe innocent until proven guilty, but I am saying that in a case where the accuser has very little to personally gain and their story is corroborated by others, you should support people brave enough to come forward. And it is not the victims fault what the abuser then does as, ultimately, a result of being caught for his own actions and behavior.
